title: Im Mai geht es nicht
desc: Saying no to somebody who is allowed to ask
setting: A Sunday telephone call at six, and a date that has stopped being far away.

steps.speaker: Deine Mutter
steps.es: Die zweite Woche im Mai. Zehn Tage. Ich habe schon geschaut.
steps.en: The second week in May. Ten days. I have already had a look.

options.feedback: Plain, and first. Everything else comes after it and none of it is an excuse.

options.es: Im Mai habe ich sehr viel im Büro.
options.en: In May I have a lot on at the office.
options.feedback: Almost true, which is what makes it an excuse. She will come back to it.

options.en: Ten days is a long time.
options.feedback: It is the real problem and it lands as a complaint about her.

options.es: Seit Januar ist zu viel passiert.
options.en: Since January too much has happened.
options.feedback: The truth, in six words. She is sixty-seven and she understands it immediately.
The second excuse in one call. Now the first one is not believed either.
Honest, and it leaves her holding a no with nothing in it.
A no with a date is an appointment. A no without one is a door.
Vielleicht means no here, and it leaves her waiting for it.

options.es: Ich melde mich, wenn es besser geht.
options.en: I will let you know when things are better.
options.feedback: Kind, and it puts the whole thing back on your side of the table.

steps.speaker: Deine Mutter
steps.es: Und? Geht es der Selina gut?

options.es: Ja. Sie fragt jede Woche nach dir.
options.en: Yes. She asks about you every week.
options.feedback: She changed the subject, which means it is settled. Go with her.
She is not. Asking makes the no into something that has to be defended.

options.es: Es tut mir wirklich leid wegen dem Mai.
options.en: I am really sorry about May.
options.feedback: Once was enough. Twice starts taking it back.
